title: Common-target section-homology diagram for composition of module f-maps
statement: Let h:X→Y and k:Y→Z be scheme morphisms, H, G, F modules on Z, Y, X, and psi:H→k_*G and phi:G→h_*F. Let Ck, Ch, Cc be choice systems of [def-weil-pbc-module-cohomology-fmap] for psi, phi, and psi followed by k_*phi and the canonical successive-pushforward comparison. Fix p≥0. Write HX, HY, HZ for global sections on complexes followed by forgetting scalars, and Hp for degree-p homology. Write bc=Hp(HZ(Cc.beta)), bk=Hp(HZ(Ck.beta)), bh=Hp(HY(Ch.beta)), mc=Hp(Cc.a followed by HZ(Cc.lambda)), mk=Hp(Ck.a followed by HZ(Ck.lambda)), mh=Hp(Ch.a followed by HY(Ch.lambda)). Let i=Hp(HX(desc id from Cc.I to Ch.I)), j=Hp(HZ(desc id from Cc.J to Ck.J)), and g=Hp(HY(desc id from Ck.I to Ch.J)). There exist an abelian group Q, qk:Hp(HZ(Ck.K))→Q, qc:Hp(HZ(Cc.K))→Q, and an isomorphism s:Hp(HY(Ch.K))→Q such that bc followed by qc equals j followed by bk and qk, mc followed by qc equals i followed by mh and s, and mk followed by qk equals g followed by bh and s.

proof.text: Reuse nat_complex_injective_resolution from ModuleCohomologyFMap through a proof-only import all. It extends by zero, applies the lower-bound-zero Mathlib injective replacement, and truncates back to obtain L and mu. Reuse nat_quasiIso_globalSections_pushforward_injectives from the same module to obtain QuasiIso Gamma(mu). Its canonical pushforward_sections_iso followed by Gamma(mu) induces an isomorphism s on homology.

Reuse lift_nat_quasiIso from ModuleCohomologyFMapComparison through a proof-only import all. Apply it to Ck.lambda and Cc.lambda with termwise injective target L, and the desired routes gamma=k_*(desc id followed by Ch.beta) followed by mu and delta=(kh)_*(desc id) followed by the inverse pushforwardComp comparison, k_*(Ch.lambda), and mu. The existing helper uses extension by zero and K-injective Qh_map_bijective to obtain maps e and f and the two lambda homotopies. No duplicate lifting theorem, mapping cylinder or monicity is needed.

Construct maps eta and xi from H concentrated in degree zero to k_*Ck.I and (kh)_*Cc.I, respectively, using fromSingle₀Equiv and the augmentation cycle equations. The compatibility fields identify Ck.J.augmentation followed by beta with eta followed by lambda, and likewise for Cc with xi. Identity descents commute with augmentations. In degree zero, the descent equations, Ch.compatible, and naturality and inverse cancellation of pushforwardComp give xi followed by delta = eta followed by gamma. Precompose the two lambda homotopies with xi and eta and concatenate to obtain a homotopy after Cc.J.augmentation. Apply the existing unique_nat_quasiIso helper from ModuleCohomologyFMapComparison across this augmentation quasi-isomorphism to obtain the beta homotopy; the helper implements extension by zero, homotopy uniqueness and ofExtend.

Reuse the canonical pushforward_sections_iso from ModuleCohomologyFMap, which uses presheaf.mapIso on inverse-image top equality. Its inverse components match each data system a by the sections field. Naturality follows componentwise from presheaf-morphism naturality. Composition follows by canceling the three isomorphisms, using pushforwardComp_inv_app_app, pushforward_obj_presheaf_map, functoriality of restriction and subsingleton morphisms of opens. Apply global sections and homology to all three homotopies; functoriality and the two proved sections identities give the three stated squares. Take Q=Hp(Gamma(Z,L)), qk=Hp(Gamma(e)), qc=Hp(Gamma(f)), and s=Hp(a(k,Ch.K) followed by Gamma(mu)). No derived-cohomology transport is used in the conclusion.

lean.statement: theorem moduleCohomologyFMap_comp_data {X Y Z : Scheme.{u}} (h : X ⟶ Y) (k : Y ⟶ Z) {H : Z.Modules} {G : Y.Modules} {F : X.Modules} (ψ : H ⟶ (pushforward k).obj G) (φ : G ⟶ (pushforward h).obj F) (Ck : ModuleCohomologyFMapData k H G ψ) (Ch : ModuleCohomologyFMapData h G F φ) (Cc : ModuleCohomologyFMapData (h ≫ k) H F (ψ ≫ (pushforward k).map φ ≫ (pushforwardComp h k).hom.app F)) (p : ℕ) : let HX := (RingedSpace.globalSectionsFunctor X.toRingedSpace ⋙ forget₂ _ AddCommGrpCat.{u}).mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℕ) let HY := (RingedSpace.globalSectionsFunctor Y.toRingedSpace ⋙ forget₂ _ AddCommGrpCat.{u}).mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℕ) let HZ := (RingedSpace.globalSectionsFunctor Z.toRingedSpace ⋙ forget₂ _ AddCommGrpCat.{u}).mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℕ) let Hp := HomologicalComplex.homologyFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{u} (ComplexShape.up ℕ) p ∃ (Q : AddCommGrpCat.{u}) (qk : Hp.obj (HZ.obj Ck.K) ⟶ Q) (qc : Hp.obj (HZ.obj Cc.K) ⟶ Q) (s : Hp.obj (HY.obj Ch.K) ⟶ Q), IsIso s ∧ Hp.map (HZ.map Cc.β) ≫ qc = Hp.map (HZ.map (InjectiveResolution.desc (𝟙 H) Ck.J Cc.J)) ≫ Hp.map (HZ.map Ck.β) ≫ qk ∧ Hp.map (Cc.a.hom ≫ HZ.map Cc.lambda) ≫ qc = Hp.map (HX.map (InjectiveResolution.desc (𝟙 F) Ch.I Cc.I)) ≫ Hp.map (Ch.a.hom ≫ HY.map Ch.lambda) ≫ s ∧ Hp.map (Ck.a.hom ≫ HZ.map Ck.lambda) ≫ qk = Hp.map (HY.map (InjectiveResolution.desc (𝟙 G) Ch.J Ck.I)) ≫ Hp.map (HY.map Ch.β) ≫ s
